title: Bytes that repeat for a routing run

blocks.text: A parcel company's routing service must give the same routes every time it reruns a day, and its determinism test compares run records from fresh processes. Compared as they are, two records never match: each holds the time the run started and how long it took, its cost carries floating-point noise, and its set of unserved stops prints in whatever order the process's hash seed gives.
The docstring of `run_bytes.py` gives a record's shape. Write:

items: `canonical(record)`, the record as bytes that are equal exactly when two runs did the same work: without the two clock fields (`started_at`, and `wall_seconds` inside `stats`), with every float rounded to 6 decimals and `-0.0` written as `0.0`, with dictionary keys sorted, each set as a sorted list, and each list kept in its order, since a route visits its stops in order;
`repeats(records)`, `True` when every record in the list has the same canonical bytes.

blocks.text: `json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))` writes compact JSON with sorted keys; JSON has no sets, so turn them into lists first. About fifteen lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from run_bytes import canonical, repeats

first = {"started_at": "2031-05-04T07:15:00", "stats": {"wall_seconds": 0.8, "nodes": 22}, "cost": 377.25,
         "routes": {"van1": ["hub", "p", "q", "hub"], "van2": ["hub", "r", "hub"]}, "unserved": {"s", "t"}}
again = {**first, "started_at": "2031-05-05T18:40:00", "stats": {"wall_seconds": 2.1, "nodes": 22},
         "cost": 377.2500000003, "unserved": {"t", "s"}}
swapped = {**first, "routes": {**first["routes"], "van1": ["hub", "q", "p", "hub"]}}

print("canonical bytes:", canonical(first))
print("next day, other clock:", repeats([first, again]))
print("van1 visits q before p:", repeats([first, swapped]))

cases.says: two runs that differ only in when they started repeat, and two that put a stop on another truck do not
the wall-clock seconds inside the stats are a clock too, while the node count is real work
a cost that differs in the tenth decimal is the same cost, and one that differs by a cent is not
-0.0 and 0.0 are the same number, though their text differs
a route visits its stops in order, so the same stops in another order is a different run

origin.section: A Determinism Test Must Be Able to Fail

concepts: a determinism comparison must tell real differences from noise, or it can never fail
runs are compared as canonical bytes, with clocks left out and floats rounded
